hook.line: Your order from a supplier arrived broken, and a chatty message will not get your money back. Spanish letters run on a few fixed, polite phrases, and once you know them you can write to any company.
hook.es: Me dirijo a ustedes para presentar una queja.
hook.en: I am writing to you all to make a complaint.

examples.es: Me dirijo a ustedes para presentar una queja.
examples.en: I am writing to you all to make a complaint.

examples.es: Me dirijo a usted para solicitar información.
examples.en: I am writing to you (formal, one person) to request information.

examples.es: Le agradecería que me respondiera antes del viernes.
examples.en: I would be grateful if you (formal) replied to me before Friday.

I look forward to your reply (a woman writing).

rule:
A formal letter has three moves.

Open: *Me dirijo a usted(es) para* + infinitive. It says who you are writing to and why.

Ask: *Le agradecería que* + a past form of the verb: *respondiera*, *enviara*, *arreglara*. English says "I would be grateful if you replied"; Spanish uses the same idea, with *agradecería* for "would be grateful" and the *-ra* form for "replied". Use *Les* when writing to several people.

Close: *Adjunto le envío…* for attachments, and *Quedo atento/a a su respuesta* to wait politely.

Always *usted*, never *tú*. Pick a *tú* tone and the letter stops sounding formal.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the imperfect subjunctive after a conditional: the softest way to make a request in writing.

options: I am writing to you all to request information.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Le agradecería que me ___ antes del viernes.* (*respondiera* or *responde*) I would be grateful if you (formal) replied to me before Friday.
yourTurn.answer: Le agradecería que me respondiera antes del viernes.
yourTurn.why: After *le agradecería que*, the verb takes the past *-ra* form.

yourTurn.prompt: Say, writing to one person (formal): I am writing to you to request information.
yourTurn.answer: Me dirijo a usted para solicitar información.
yourTurn.why: *Me dirijo a usted para* opens a letter to one person.

yourTurn.prompt: Say, writing to a company (you all): I am writing to you to make a complaint.
yourTurn.answer: Me dirijo a ustedes para presentar una queja.
accept: Me dirijo a ustedes para presentar una queja
yourTurn.why: A company is several people, so *ustedes*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say, writing to one person (formal): I would be grateful if you sent me a copy of the contract.
yourTurn.answer: Le agradecería que me enviara una copia del contrato.
yourTurn.why: *Le agradecería que* plus *enviara* is the polite request.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it for a company (you all): *Le agradecería que me respondiera antes del viernes.*
yourTurn.answer: Les agradecería que me respondieran antes del viernes.
yourTurn.why: With several readers, both *les* and the verb go plural.

yourTurn.prompt: Say, a man writing: I look forward to your reply.
yourTurn.why: *Atento* ends in *-o* for a man and *-a* for a woman.

yourTurn.prompt: Say, you enclose your résumé for one person (formal).
yourTurn.answer: Adjunto le envío mi hoja de vida.
yourTurn.why: *Adjunto le envío* is the stock phrase for attachments.

pitfalls.wrong: Le agradecería que me responde antes del viernes.
pitfalls.right: Le agradecería que me respondiera antes del viernes.
pitfalls.why: Almost. A polite request in writing needs the past *-ra* form, not the present.

pitfalls.wrong: Me dirijo usted para solicitar información.
pitfalls.right: Me dirijo a usted para solicitar información.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Dirigirse* needs *a* before the person you are writing to.

pitfalls.wrong: Te agradecería que me respondieras antes del viernes.
pitfalls.right: Le agradecería que me respondiera antes del viernes.
pitfalls.why: Almost. A formal letter uses *usted*, so *le* and *respondiera*.

pitfalls.wrong: Escribo a ustedes para presentar una queja.
pitfalls.right: Me dirijo a ustedes para presentar una queja.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Escribo a* is correct but too plain; letters open with *me dirijo a*.

personal: Write the opening of a letter you might send this week: who it is for, and what you are asking, using *Me dirijo a…* and *Le agradecería que…*.
